verses.text: Bezalel made the ark out of acacia wood. It was about one metre and ten centimetres long, and about seventy centimetres wide and seventy centimetres high.
He covered it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold border around it.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
Then he made poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
He made the cover, the place of mercy, out of pure gold. It was about one metre and ten centimetres long and seventy centimetres wide.
He made two cherubim out of hammered gold for the two ends of the cover,
one cherub on one end and the other cherub on the other end. He made the cherubim and the cover all one piece.
The cherubim had their wings spread upwards, covering the cover with their wings. They faced each other, looking down towards the cover.
He made the table out of acacia wood. It was about ninety centimetres long, forty-five centimetres wide, and seventy centimetres high.
He covered it with pure gold and put a gold border around it.
He made a rim around it about as wide as a hand, and put a gold border on the rim.
He cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners, where the four legs were.
The rings were close to the rim, to hold the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles out of acacia wood and covered them with gold, to carry the table.
He made the things for the table out of pure gold: its plates, dishes, bowls, and jars for pouring out drink offerings.
He made the lampstand out of pure gold. He hammered out its base and its stem. Its flower-shaped cups, buds, and blossoms were all one piece with it.
Six branches came out from the sides of the lampstand, three on one side and three on the other.
Each of the six branches had three cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms, on one branch and on the other branch.
And on the lampstand itself there were four cups shaped like almond flowers, with buds and blossoms.
One bud was under the first pair of branches, a second bud under the second pair, and a third bud under the third pair. All six branches came out from the lampstand.
The buds and the branches were all one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its wick cutters, and its trays out of pure gold.
He used about thirty-four kilograms of pure gold to make the lampstand and all its tools.
He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, about forty-five centimetres long and forty-five centimetres wide, and about ninety centimetres high. Its horns were one piece with it.
He covered the top, all the sides, and the horns with pure gold, and put a gold border around it.
He made two gold rings below the border, on the two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and covered them with gold.
He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, sweet-smelling incense, the work of a perfume maker.
